newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent closes up on lower loadings, but off high.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent closes up on lower loadings, but off high.

text.p: IPE Brent futures closed higher on Thursday, but off earlier highs inspired by a lower-than-expected physical Brent loading programme for April as last minute profit-taking ate into gains, traders said.
The April contract settled 28 cents higher at $19.89 a barrel against an intra-day high of $20.02. May closed just three cents up at $19.41.
April gas oil settled $1.75 higher at $169.00 a tonne.
"I don't think many players had the courage to stay in above the $20 level," one trader said.
"This market is still looking for selling opportunities," said another. "It's not on the up and up yet."
Traders said the gains had been inspired initially by a lower-than-expected Brent loading programme for April.
The programme was the equivalent of eight full 500,000 barrel cargoes less than March.
Looking at the three loading programmes released so far -- Brent, Forties and Flota -- this equals a 120,000 barrel per day reduction in output.
Traders said the bullish effect of the smaller programme had been heightened by the fact the April contract expires on Friday.
"With the expiry tomorrow prompt delivery material looks a bit tight," said one trader. "We could see a bit of a squeeze going on."
